articleTitle: TacForce: From Images to Tactile Force Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: This paper introduces TacForce, a camera-based tactile sensor for robotic skin. TacForce utilizes affordable high-resolution cameras and robust image-processing techniques to provide real-time information on the three-dimensional surface shape and force distribution applied to its soft skin surface. The sensor's skin, composed of soft, elastic materials, features an array of markers tracked by a simple stereo camera. The movement of these markers in three dimensions is mapped to external forces using the finite element method (FEM). The silicone skin is cost-effective, easy to fabricate, and adaptable to various applications through adjustments to its shape and size. TacForce offers a simple, scalable structure suitable for a wide range of robot parts and tactile devices.

articleTitle: Development of Hybrid Controller for An Affordable Cart-Pole System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: A cart-pole system has been a common plant for benchmarking control algorithms because of its non-linear, under-actuated and unstable nature. The pole (or pendulum) alone can exhibit various interesting behaviors ranging from simple harmonic motion to chaotic dynamics in the case of a multi-link pendulum. The cart in a cart-pole system is the actuated component, providing a way to manipulate the pendulum by applying a control force to move the cart horizontally. In this paper, only the generic single-link-inverted-pendulum-on-a-cart is considered. The main goal of this study is to illustrate methods that can effectively model the dynamics and design a hybrid control strategy for a single-inverted-pendulum-on-a-cart system. Moreover, this paper also presents a useful workflow for not only constructing the physical system, but also implementing a control law in a cart-pole plant without the help of expensive hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) devices.

articleTitle: Competition as an Effective Motivational Tool in Online Education
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: We would like to present a pilot function of the e-Iearning framework of the University of Dunaujvaros with its renewed functionality and the benefits that can be associated with it. The sharing of online educational content and online pedagogy is becoming more and more prevalent and accepted in higher education. In order to meet the expectations of students and teachers, we are trying to use the Moodle framework as a platform for communication, knowledge acquisition and assessment. Student activity, the use of functions set up with different parameters, is administered, and statements and evaluations are made. The evaluation system will be made more enjoyable for the students by using the ranking and highlighting systems familiar in gaming software. We assess the effectiveness of the student-centeredness of the designed service, its possibilities and its motivational impact on the students, by evaluating the competitive feelings that are learned in the game basics. In this study, we discuss the results obtained after the introduction of the new system and the conclusions that can be drawn from them. Of note is the change in the amount of measurable activity in the framework and the distribution of the types of content clickable. In the concluding part of the paper, we will focus on further development directions, as well as on connected services and directions for further development, and try to make suggestions. The further development described in the paper is basically a successful implementation of the competitive motivation measurement, but further fine-tuning and linked services are needed.

articleTitle: Comparative Evaluation of Machine Learning and Bayesian Deep Learning Methods for Estimating Ultimate Recovery in Shale Well Reservoirs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: The Estimated Ultimate Recovery (EUR) is an important parameter in oil and gas production resources, particularly in hydrocarbon-rich shale wells. This study shows EUR prediction using three algorithms: Group Method of Data Handling (GMDH), Lasso, and Bayesian Deep Learning (BDL). The dataset includes 2200 data records from 15 shale gas wells, divided into 70% for training, 15% for testing, and 15% for validation. After the evaluation of three algorithms, the BDL algorithm has higher accuracy than the other algorithms. This algorithm has advantages such as providing quantitative prediction uncertainty assessment, resilience to outliers, adaptability to complex relationships, intrinsic regularization, transfer learning, ensemble formation, handling of heteroscedasticity, integration into active learning, and improved model interpretability. The results obtained using the test data for the BDL algorithm include a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 4.2691 m3 and an R-squared (R2) value of 0.9879. Based on the findings of this study, it is suggested that researchers utilize this algorithm to predict key parameters.

articleTitle: Generative Neural Models in Robotics: Pioneering the Embodied AI Revolution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: The concept of machines with the capability for self-reproduction and the creation of useful artifacts has intrigued thinkers like John von Neumann, whose seminal contributions continue to influence contemporary technology. Yet, the modern discourse has evolved, emphasizing machines' autonomous performance of beneficial tasks over self-replication. This shift is markedly noticeable in domains such as transportation, elderly care, household management, and manufacturing, where the past decade has witnessed a gradual but consistent advancement. This progress is characterized by innovations in specialized tasks and tools, which, however, lack integration into a cohesive universal framework. Conversely, the growth in AI fields not inherently tied to physical interaction has seen an exponential rise, fueled by significant increases in the resources allocated for developing neural models. This surge has led to groundbreaking commercial innovations in textual, visual, and auditory content generation becoming widely accessible in remarkably short times. Yet, the question remains: How do these advances in generative AI translate to the physical realm, particularly in enhancing robotic capabilities? My presentation delves into this inquiry, analyzing it through the prism of cutting-edge research and emerging trends, aiming to shed light on how generative neural models are spearheading the revolution in Embodied AI.

articleTitle: The Determinants That Impact Customer Purchase Intention in the Context of Exercise Equipment Live Streaming
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: This study focuses on an under-researched aspect of e-commerce live streaming: the growing demand for fitness equipment, especially in response to the increased focus on health due to the COVID-19 epidemic. This research diverges from existing literature by specifically examining the effects of live streaming fitness equipment, a sector that has become increasingly popular due to the pandemic-driven surge in health and fitness consciousness. While previous studies primarily explore the overall influence of e-commerce live streaming on consumer purchase intentions, this research narrows its focus to the fitness equipment niche. The research utilizes a semi-structured interview method, with 15 participants from China, and applies grounded theory methodology for analysis. The study reveals that consumer purchase intentions in the context of fitness equipment live streaming are complex, influenced by eight crucial factors: streamer professionalism, main streaming similarity, streamer interactivity, entertainment, preferential, information quality, product quality, and product appearance. These findings address a vacuum in academic research on live streaming in the exercise equipment sector and provide valuable information for digital marketing strategists and business owners in the quickly changing e-commerce ecosystem.

articleTitle: Interpreting the Meaning of Agility, Perceiving its Individual Importance Through the Eyes of Different Generations1
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Agility - like the XXI. one of the fashionable concepts and leading approaches of the 20th century - it came into the spotlight after the 2000s. At first, as a new project management methodology, it was included in the thinking, which is able to eliminate the shortcomings and slowness of the classic waterfall model, thus making project management more efficient, directing them towards successful projects. Seeing the success of agile project management, more and more companies and businesses began to agileize their various organizational units as well, and finally the mindset spread to the whole organization. Today, we interpret the concept of agility not only at the organizational level, but also at the individual level. However, the willingness of individuals and employees to agility differs along a number of factors. It is influenced by an individual's age, generation affiliation, education, culture, which determines the extent to which he or she is able to embrace this new way of thinking. In our study, we look for the answer to what agility means as a term in the reading of respondents of each generation. The basis of our study is a questionnaire research carried out in Hungary, which was also part of an international research.

articleTitle: Develop A Navigation Approach for Mobile Robots Based on the Distributional Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: With traditional reinforcement learning, mobile robots can learn the expected value of each action in every state. However, in environments with uncertain situations, such as the sudden appearance of obstacles, the expected value may not accurately reflect the situation, leading to unsuccessful navigation for the robot. Distributional Deep Reinforcement Learning can help the mobile robot learn the distribution of future outcomes of actions. Instead of predicting a single expected value, the model will predict a distribution of positions that may be reached after each action. In this paper, a novel Quantile Regression Deep Q-Network (QR-DQN) algorithm is proposed to address the obstacle avoidance problem on a mobile robot based on depth images. Moreover, the designed model concentrates on integrating depth information and its application in the control system via the neuron-network sequence layers. The simulation results reveal that the proposed method outperforms the other Deep Reinforcement Learning method under different scenarios.

articleTitle: Development of Deep Learning-Based Laser Weeding Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Agriculture is an important sector that contributes significantly to Vietnam's GDP. The use of pesticides and herbicides, however, raises great concern due to their harm to the environment and human health. The government is taking action to eliminate the use of these chemicals, meanwhile, alternative solutions are needed. The aim of this paper is to develop an effective solution for weed control using a computer vision-based laser weed-killing robot. To ensure efficiency and accuracy, computer vision models must be evaluated based on different metrics such as performance, speed, and computational cost represented by mean average precision, speed of inferences (in fps), and the size of the model in FLOPs and params. The study focuses on deploying the state-of-the-art object detection model YOLOv8 on a dataset of 9,000 labeled images taken from fields in Pakistan. YOLOv8 outperforms YOLOv5 in a previous study with an accuracy of 0.9043@IOU 0.5, particularly suited for hardware efficient integration due to its 'n' and ‘s’ versions. Both models in “n” version demonstrated similar real-time frame processing times, operating at an FPS rate of approximately 62.5ms using the same computer configuration. The results show that YOLOv8n is a fitting choice for the laser weedkilling robot due to its superior weed detection capabilities.

articleTitle: Advanced Machine Learning Methods for Accurate Prediction of Loss Circulation in Drilling Well Log
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Drilling mud (DM) plays an important role for exploration of oil and gas reservoirs. Lost circulation (LC) has highly influenced drilling costs due to the waste and loss of the drilling fluid (DF), which stems from some variables such as mud composition, permeability, and mud pressure. To predict this important parameter, a dataset includes 1003 data points was collected from two oil field wells in southern Iran. For the prediction of LC in this article, three hybrid algorithms were used, combining three optimization algorithms with one network algorithm, including Social Ski-Driver (SSD), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Genetic Algorithm (GA) with the Multilayer Perceptron Network (MLP). Analysis shows the combination of the MLP with SSD give good and higher accuracy than other algorithms. The statical error meteoric for the test dataset, as indicated by an RMSE of 30.85 and an impressive R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 0.94, show their results are better and over than other competing algorithms.

articleTitle: Semi-automated Solution for Extracting Information from Images using Machine Learning methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Artificial intelligence has been more and more used in recent years, including computer-aided diagnosis systems. The published scientific papers increased exponentially, making it hard to follow new trends or to apply by a non-specialist. The goal of the present work is to present a survey of recent results in image processing and semi-automatic interpretation of information. To this end, an exhaustive analysis of the literature is carried out. To prove the concept, an implementation of a method for semi-automatic processing and extraction of information from an image using machine learning is presented for fibrosis using Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and Computed Tomography (CT). The obtained results can open new research in the field.

articleTitle: A Study on Tooth Decay Detection Using a Simple Convolutional Neural Network Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Tooth decay is a prevalent and severe oral health issue affecting individuals of all ages. Early detection and diagnosis of tooth decay are crucial for successful treatment and preventing further damage to the teeth, thereby reducing the workload for dentists. This study proposes a convolution neural network (CNN) model for early-stage tooth decay detection. The proposed CNN model is simple and includes two Convolutional layers trained with minimal parameters. In this study, some model factors were investigated to improve the accuracy of the proposed CNN model in detecting tooth decay. The results show that a CNN model with a batch size of 16 and using a dropout layer achieved an accuracy of 99.61% in detecting tooth decay, which is higher than other popular models, such as VGG19, Resnet50, and DenseNet12, in accuracy with the same dataset.

articleTitle: A Bipedal Controller Design to Realize Human Gaits
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: This research aims to mimic the exact gait of a human. In other words, we try to build a biped digital twin for human locomotion. The biped control has been a popular topic for years, and the various control methods are becoming matual. Advanced gait control for jumping, step climbing, and recovery from pushing have all been developed. Recent research has also addressed how to conduct a human-like gait. However, these results all used gaits that balance the biped instead of asking the biped to mimic the exact gait of a human. The concept can be helpful when one tries to examine if the gait of a human is normal. It can also be used to monitor the performance of an exoskeleton. The proposed digital twin analyzes the dynamic characteristics of the entire human body and determines the joint torques required for maintaining balance. This study constructed a bipedal robot model that conforms to the human body to simulate human postures. The zero moment point is used as a reference point for the interaction with the ground. We then used a cart table model to balance the bipedal robot. The controller outputs an assistive force at the center of mass position to maintain balance during walking. Finally, we convert the assistive force into ankle joint outputs to enhance gait stability and ensure that the waveform and numerical outputs are close to actual human data in the literature.

articleTitle: Optimizing Algorithmic Trading by Integrating Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: This research focuses on enhancing algorithmic trading models through the integration of sentiment analysis, employing a custom-developed Python program. The application of sentiment analysis, which evaluates the emotional tone in text data from sources such as social media, news articles, and financial reports, provides key insights into market sentiments. By incorporating these insights into algorithmic trading strategies using a Python-based program, traders and financial analysts can gain a deeper understanding of market dynamics and investor behavior. This integration leads to more informed decision-making, enhanced risk management, and the potential for increased returns on investment. The use of a customized Python program allows for targeted analysis and adaptability in processing a variety of data sources, proving to be an essential asset in this innovative approach. This research represents a significant step forward in merging the fields of finance, data science, and artificial intelligence to develop more advanced and responsive trading systems.

articleTitle: Development a Cheap Force Sensor Detecting Vibration Mode for UAV
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: An unmanned aerial vehicle is always subject to vibrations of different frequencies caused by aerodynamic forces or components such as engines, propellers. When the amplitude of these vibrations is large, the flying device can become uncontrollable, mechanical joints between parts become loose or destroyed. The determination of the frequency and amplitude of vibrations to determine the mode of vibration on the flying machine is presented in this article. The objective of the research was to build a force sensor that is cheap, efficient and easy to use. Through the analysis of the complex oscillations received from the sensor in the frequency domain to find the frequency of oscillation with the highest power, which is one of the applications of this detection early flutter. The research results show that this sensor works stably and accurately. The frequency and amplitude of the vibration are clearly evaluated.

articleTitle: Real-time Detection to Avoid Accidents of Interaction Between Humans and Collaborative Robot Using Image Processing and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: In recent years, the integration of collaborative robots, also known as cobots, into various industrial and service sectors has shown promising results in increasing productivity and efficiency. However, as these robots work alongside human operators, ensuring the safety of human-robot interactions remains a critical challenge. Accidents arising from unintended collisions or improper robot behavior can have severe consequences for both human operators and the operational environment. The safety condition for humans in the interaction space is always the most important requirement in such systems. Active collision detection to avoid accidents has been a challenge due to the uncertain cognition of humans. In this research, the real-time detection system recognizes human activities in the co-working space by applying image processing and machine learning. The system design is aimed at low cost with 2D cameras but high efficiency with up to 90% correcting detection. The results showed the potential of applying real-time detection in industries to protect humans.

articleTitle: Research on Thinning Variation of the Copper Upper Sheet in Copper-Steel Double-Sheet Hydroforming
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Sheet hydroforming has become progressively attractive in the automotive and aerospace sectors due to numerous benefits, including enhanced forming capabilities, good surface quality, and the ability to form complicated parts. A notable advantage is the simultaneous and uniform pressure distribution across the entire surface. This method makes it easier to form multi-layer sheets with complex geometries compared to conventional methods. Based on these advantages, the hydroforming of double-layer sheets for the conical part is investigated. Some features of the formed inner and outer layers, including hydraulic pressure, initial bulging pressure, wall thickness distributions are discussed in detail. Double-sheet of Cu/DC04 was selected to investigate the hydroforming process by numerical simulation method. Research results show the relationship between forming pressure and quality of 2-layer conical products. The results are meaningful in predicting shaping trends and choosing optimal technological parameters in forming sheet products using hydroforming methods.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Sytems: Some New Trends in System Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: A wide class of nonlinear systems can be described by functional series representations like Volterra- and Fliess - series. It is a known result that Volterra – series approximators as finite dimensional models for nonlinear systems can be constructed as nonlinear moving average (NLMA) operators cascaded with static polynomial nonlinearities. This motivates the use of block – oriented modeling and control of certain nonlinear systems. This talk will discuss the modeling and identification issues of frequently used block oriented (Wiener – Hammerstein) and bilinear models and some related problem like dynamic inversion and unknown input estimation. Embedding nonlinear models into linear ones (immersion) will be considered, too. An application for obtaining yaw – dynamic models for self a driving car operating at various speeds will be shown for illustration.

articleTitle: Comparison of Data Visualization Platforms Through European Traffic Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: The most important and valuable resource in the 21st century is data. The age of the internet brought us an era in which humans, within a foreseeable time, are unable to process the vast amount of data that we produce. It's important to understand the data and statistics we have because it can help a company make a well thought out decision on a given dilemma, which is based on reality and data. When choosing a data visualisation platform, the purpose of the application, the type of data and the user needs are also key factors. For the visualisation of traffic data in Europe, a number of established platforms can be considered and are referred to in this paper. This article compares data visualisation platforms currently available and used in industrial environments with open source free platforms, using European traffic data.

articleTitle: Automated Biofeedback Processing: A Robust API Development Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: The aim of this paper was to design and develop a system for collecting and evaluating biofeedback using smart devices while maintaining non- invasiveness. Multiple smart devices were analysed in the research such as smart bracelets and smart blood pressure monitors. This work included the creation of a user interface and a web application for visualizing and analysing the collected data. The accuracy of the obtained data was verified using professional medical devices under the supervision of a medical doctor. The paper also focuses on network communication and the application programming interface (API). The resulting system provides valuable insights into an individual's vital signs, contributing to the field of healthcare and wellness.

articleTitle: Generation Z Motivations at Work Based on Primary Findings Among Chinese Youth
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Job choice and retention are of paramount importance, especially in today's labour market conditions. Job selection criteria have changed significantly, further differentiated by generational differences and characteristics. Rather than standard solutions, employers need to think in terms of employer branding and HR strategies based on expectations tailored to individual career path needs. In this paper, we present the results of primary research conducted in a Chinese market, focusing specifically on Generation Z. With an international perspective, we analyse the perceptions of young Chinese people and evaluate the practical application of tools and methods to motivate them in HR and employer branding.

articleTitle: ChatGPT and Large Language Models in Healthcare; a Bibliometrics Analysis and Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: ChatGPT and similar large language models (LLMs) are becoming the essential tools in healthcare, offering diverse applications. This article presents a bibliometric analysis for studying the dimension and the role of ChatGPT and major large language models in healthcare. The LLMs’ impact, usage, and growth in medical literature is presented. Through exploring the Scopus database, this article uncovers the trends and contributions of LLMs. Our findings deliver insights into the evolution of the LLMs’ applications highlighting their significance and limitations in shaping future healthcare.

articleTitle: Design a Controller for Parallel Robot Using GA and Fuzzy Type-2 Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: This paper provides a trajectory control rule for delta robots based on an Interval Type-2 Fuzzy Logic Controller (IT2FLC) optimized by using a Genetic Algorithm (GA). The IT2FLC is created utilizing the fuzzy logic approach of Type-1 Fuzzy Logic Controllers (T1FLC). GA is used for the controller's pre-processing. The proposed controller is used for the Delta robot in different cases such as without disturbance, with disturbance, and with load. The paper compares the simulation results to those of T1FLC and PID controllers. According to the results, IT2FLC outperforms the other controllers in terms of tracking control trajectory.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Classification Using Convolutional Neural Networks and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Image classification represents a widely researched current topic, with hundreds of applications in medical imaging. The classification of brain tumors cannot be an exception, it is an applications where various machine learning techniques have been tried out already and convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures lead the benchmark records. Several brain MRI datasets were involved in the search of the best performing CNN, and these studies found better and better solutions for a specific set of data. In this paper we propose a CNN architecture which is trained and tested on three different datasets, including classification problems of two, three, and four classes, with the only architectural difference of using one neuron for each class in the output layer of the fully connected network part. The proposed network produced classifications of fine accuracy, with misclassification rates of 1.1 %, 2 %, and 4 %, when deployed in the two-class, three-class, and four-class classification problems, respectively. These benchmarks indicate that the proposed network can compete with state-of-the-art solutions. There are still several open directions for further optimization of the decision making system.

articleTitle: ICT and Telecommunications Supply Chain: Threat Landscape and Countermeasures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: The Information and Communications Technology and the Telecommunications supply chain are converging due to the expansion of new technologies, including 5G networks. This work details the elements in these supply chains, focusing on telecommunications. It also examines the different threats and challenges faced by the telecom supply chain. Finally, it presents solutions and recommendations for enhancing security levels across the digital supply chain.

articleTitle: Bifurcations and Application of the Vallis – Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Investigating chaotic systems is a fertile field considering that chaos is an exotic chapter in the theory of differential equations, and it has useful applications in the theory of communications. In this work a well-known chaotic system is investigated from the bifurcation point of view and some applications are also introduced. The data studied are also visualized for better clarity. The results observed can be helpful in the encryption methods of the implementation of different communication channels.

articleTitle: Development of Cutting Tool Selection Module for 2.5D Pocket Machining
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: For CNC machining of a pocket, the selection of cutting tool set significantly affects the machining efficiency especially on rough machining. However, there is no selection module integrated in CAD/CAM software to consider this problem. This paper presents an effective method in selecting the optimal tool set for machining 2.5D pockets based on the main geometry information of the 2.5D pocket. The proposed algorithm focuses on several important factors such as machining time and cutting tool cost. The automatic selection module can yield a “near-optimal” the cutting tool set for 2.5D pocket machining from the specific cutting tool database. An example is presented to validate the uitility performmace, effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: AIoT and Its Applications: Industry and Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Through several waves of ups and downs in the past decades, artificial intelligence (AI) has evolved into a must-have new technology or tool in various domains. Furthermore, with the advent of powerful GPU, AI-related research or AI-based applications have sprouted in every corner of the world. Originating from pure network connectivity, the Internet of Things (IoT) has become a structure that can collect every piece of data from physical devices, daily activities, images, or videos into a data reservoir. As a result, tons of data are automatically generated into an enterprise database in a single day. This creates research opportunities on integrating AI, IoT, big data, and cloud or edge computing, to improve the quality of industrial production or medical service. Applications of AI algorithms, fuzzy modeling, and/or intelligent systems play important roles and can be found everywhere, including widespread usage in industry and medical systems for tasks such as locating and detecting scratches or defects in product surface, printed circuit board manufacturing, monitoring rehabilitation progress for patients with Parkinson's disease or stroke, autonomous moving and planning of service robots in healthcare, and short-term or long-term prediction of air quality in certain areas. Furthermore, AI can be integrated with other techniques, such as Internet of things, fuzzy modeling, and edge computing to become powerful tools for industry and medicine domains. This talk will address from the AIoT, fuzzy modeling and system engineering perspective for applications faced in industry and healthcare.

articleTitle: Analysis of Mechanical Faults of Asynchronous Motors Based on the Abrasion Map
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: The target area of the research is the assessment of the mechanical excitation frequencies of three-phase asynchronous motors, primarily caused by bearing and shaft adjustment, and the understanding of the wear process. Measurements and calculations are basically based on a wear map, not only using spectrum analysis methods. Spectrum analyzes do not solve the steps for developing fault detection methods in all cases. The processing of measurement results was preceded by several measurement cycles, the results of which were used to create the wear map.

articleTitle: Learning Medical Subject Headings in PubMed Articles to Enhance Deep Predictions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: MeSH is a vocabulary of terms used in the life sciences and biomedical fields. A large amount of Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) occur in PubMed articles with different weights. In this research, we analyze a disease-symptom network exploiting MeSH metadata co-occurring in 7 million PubMed articles and configure a deep model in the context of biomedical and health care data. Optimized and efficient data networks are important to compile machine learning models. We optimize the deep model by reducing important features. Our result highlights that the degree of the severity of symptoms associated with a disease improves the accuracy of disease prediction models. The network was well optimized by reducing the number of symptoms. This finding may have important implications in healthcare: healthcare chatbots, clinical significance, practical implications.

articleTitle: An Efficient Improved A* Algorithm for Mobile Robot Path Planning in Complex Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: This paper presents an improved path planning algorithm specifically designed for mobile robots operating in complex environments with a mix of small and large obstacles. Building upon the widely used A* algorithm, the focus of this approach lies in achieving a balance between fast computation and optimal path length. To evaluate its performance, a simulation system was created, and a custom map was designed. Through extensive simulations, a comparative analysis of the popular path planning algorithms, including RRT, RRT*, A*, and the proposed algorithm, was conducted. The simulation results clearly show that the developed algorithm outperforms the others in terms of computation speed and stability. These findings highlight the effectiveness of the proposed approach and its potential for practical use in real-world applications involving mobile robots.

articleTitle: Subjective Haptics: Sharing and Augmentation of Sensorimotor Control: Plenary Talk
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Haptic sensation depends on our bodies as well as an object touched. Mechanical interaction between the skin and object derives haptic sensations and individual skin characteristics and movements influence haptic sensations. Furthermore, the movement is consciously or unconsciously adjusted by the haptic sensation. Thus, haptic sensation involves individual physical skill, indicating that haptic technologies reflecting individual sensorimotor controls might be available not only for object recognition but also for human augmentation. We have developed a wearable tactile sensor that allows a user to touch an object with their bare fingertip and measure subjective tactile sensations. Integrating it with the tactile feedback interface can be available to enhance tactile sensation, improve motor skills, share tactile sensations with others, and human-human/robot collaborations. In addition, we have investigated body integration through a robotic avatar in which multiple users cooperate. We have observed the effect of improving the operation and sense of agency in body integration, indicating that embodied collaboration can overcome individual abilities. Under these research and developments, the design of haptic interfaces for integrating sensory information with motor information is crucial in inducing intuitive recognition and operation, promoting collaboration, and improving a sense of agency. I will introduce interfaces and systems developed and findings, and discuss future applications and challenges using individual haptic sensations.

articleTitle: Federated Learning for Offensive Security in Cyber-Medical Systems Inspired by Petri Nets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Federated learning is a machine learning method that allows models to be trained on decentralised data without participants sharing it with a central server. Federated learning can be modelled using Petri nets, mathematical models for sequence sequences. Devices train on their own data and send model updates to a central server. The central server averages the updates and returns the global model to the devices. The devices then update their local models using the global model.

articleTitle: Intelligent Computing Integrated Autonomous Model of Research
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Highly automated engineering achievements (EAs) are increasingly developed and operated using active model representations to achieve reactive and autonomous behaviors mainly at situation recognition based decision and execution. This paper is contribution to research in the above purposed model which can be enough comprehensive, large, and extensive to serve complete research owing to among others the model integration efforts during the past decades. Model integration is highly based on intelligent computing theories, methodologies and systemic in a multidisciplinary, multiphysics, and cyber physical scenario. In this paper, the author first introduces and explains the model mediated research (MMR) to support research using integrated experimental model of the actual research (IEMR). IEMR is developed as analytic and behavioral model with extensive using of knowledge representations. Contributions to IEMR are developed and organized in collaborative space (CS) of the actual project on the cloud for lifecycle of research. Role of CS is essential to ensure contribution to research independently of organizational and geographic position of participants. MMR based research using IEMR in CS is recently realized at the Virtual Research Laboratory (VRL) on suitably configured engineering modeling platform (EMP). VRL is active in the organization of the Doctoral School of Applied Informatics and Applied Mathematics. It applies own cloud platform in the 3DEXPERIRNCE platform by the Dassault Systémes S. A. This platform is specifically configured for the purpose of PhD research.

Author Keywords: research in collaborative space on the cloud

articleTitle: Parametric Study on Geometry of T-Coupling in Micro-Extrusion Process
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Micro forming is undergoing significant development with substantial advancements in both equipment and technology. This progress is evident in industries such as electronics, automation, automotive, aerospace, medical, and chemistry. One of the major challenges of micro forming processes compared to conventional forming methods is the micro-scale of particles. This paper presents evaluations and insights into some factors which influence the forming ability and the quality of T-joint connections in micro-extrusion technology. The factors investigated in this paper include the geometric shape of the die, friction, and temperature. Consequently, a suitable set of geometric parameters and the most suitable, optimized equipment can be established for practical production of T-joint components by using the micro-extrusion technology, aiming to create products with the desired shape and dimensions as required.

articleTitle: Blockchain Applications in AI and Security (Case Study HealthCare)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Evidentially, the development of BlockchainBlockchain- and AI-based paradigms is moving forward at a breakneck pace. Although both models provide something original to the market, their levels of complexity and innovation vary. Blockchains may automate payments in the era of digital currency to enable the secure cryptocurrency exchange of private information, information, and records[1]. Two of the most discussed technologies are artificial intelligence and blockchains. Blockchain technology enables automating Bitcoin payments and provides individuals access to a distributed ledger of documents, transactions, and information. Blockchain technology can control user interactions using smart contracts without a demand for a centralized authority. As a substitute, artificial intelligence (AI) gives machines decision-making and reasoning capabilities comparable to those of humans. This revelation resulted from a detailed analysis of the BlockchainBlockchain and artificial intelligence combination developed between 2012 and the beginning of 2024. This critical analysis includes 290 papers over the last ten to eleven years examining the current state and justification for artificial intelligence, machine learning, and blockchain combo. The focus of the meatiest part of this study is the actual implementation of the integration. Additionally, with an emphasis on the limitations, gaps, and issues of this combined application in the related literature, they have been researched using bibliometrics analysis, and other intentions have been made to research future applications connecting BlockchainBlockchain and AI in the healthcare industry.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of PD Controllers Using BCMO Algorithm for Active Control of Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Reducing harmful vibrations of structures by active control devices using different control algorithms is an exciting ​​research area with many important applications. The present work introduces a simple approach to optimally design a Proportional-Derivative (PD) controller for active control of structures. The control force is obtained using a control gain vector and all system state variables. The PD controller is optimized using the elements of the control gain vector as the design variables to minimize the system's relative displacement and absolute acceleration using the Balancing composite motion optimization (BCMO) algorithm. The optimal constraints include the stability of the system and the average control force (related to the system's control energy). The studied model is a 3-story building structure subjected to earthquake loads. The simulation results show that the proposed controllers have high efficiency, ensure stability, and require low control energy compared to the results of a controller in a published study.

articleTitle: Main Challenges of a Research, Development and Innovation Project in the Academic Sector
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Innovation, and within it research and development, is the engine of progress and sustainability in today's world. The academic sector is a key cornerstone of this activity. This publication addresses the challenges and strengths of innovation projects and project management, particularly in the context of the academic sector. It analyses the concept of innovation, the characteristics of R&D activities and distinguishes between innovation and R&D. It presents the generations of innovation models and the characteristics and challenges of innovation projects, such as the management of technological uncertainty, financing difficulties and the application of project management methodology. It points out that the success of innovation projects depends to a large extent on the choice of an appropriate project management approach that takes into account the non-linear nature of innovation and allows for adaptation to the different project contexts.

articleTitle: The Impact of the Inflationary Environment on Individuals' Financial Culture and Purchasing Decisions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: In today's world, it is increasingly challenging to make financially sound, forward-looking decisions. Since the 1990s, the services offered by the financial market have gradually expanded, requiring more and more knowledge to make a major decision. The 2008 economic crisis showed that society has very little and incomplete knowledge of how financial instruments and products work. After the 2008 economic crisis, there has been a gradual increase in the attention paid to financial literacy/culture research targeting younger generations, trying to find out the correlation between financial literacy, financial behaviours seen in the family and long-term financial well-being. National leaders and economic actors have realised that they can build a financially stable society for the future by starting financial education at a young age. The current generation, aged between 18 and 35, is the generation that has already learned basic financial skills at least in secondary school, and this influences their future financial decisions. The past year has seen unprecedented inflation in the world and in our country, and this scale of change has had a major impact on the lives of the younger generation. In this study, we explore the extent to which young people have been able to overcome the financial obstacles caused by inflation and how their financial culture has changed in the light of a questionnaire survey conducted in Hungary.

articleTitle: Proposing to Use Backstepping Controller for Sitting/Lying Type Lower Limb Rehabilitation Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: The WHO predicts that by 2050 the total number of elderly people will double, accompanied by an increase in related diseases. As life becomes more modern and convenient, the average age lengthens and the number of elderly people increases. The post-injury rehabilitation process has been developed for many years, but the human resources for that process are too small, leading to a situation where many patients do not receive proper treatment. From there, we see an essential need for lower limb rehabilitation. This study focuses on studying the controller for the sitting/lying rehabilitation robot being developed. The research process starts from collecting documents on robot control models for lower limb rehabilitation and the most suitable input trajectories. The research processed starts from collecting documents on robot control models for lower limb rehabilitation and the most suitable input trajectories. After that, the research would go into applying the Backstepping control method to the Robot, through fine-tuning the coefficients and experimenting with different step cycles. These experimental results are compared with the case of using PID controller and Backstepping controller, showing significantly better quality.

articleTitle: Microeconomic Factors Affecting Competitiveness Based on the Opinion of Hungarian Companies1
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: As economic complexity intensifies, competitiveness appears as a dynamic concept that transcends the boundaries of industries and national economies. In addition to mere market share or profitability, competitiveness is a truly multifaceted concept that examines the essential elements that determine success in a given environment. It includes addressing challenges effectively, identifying and exploiting opportunities, and reaping sustainable benefits. As a concept, competitiveness is not static, evolving in response to changing market dynamics, technological advances, and changing consumer preferences. This study offers an opportunity to explore the fundamental context of competitiveness and, above all, to establish a link between microeconomic factors and the evolution of competitiveness. In addition to the literature review, the results of a primary research will be presented. This research seeks to find answers to which of the factors affecting the competitiveness of Hungarian enterprises can be directly related to the change in microeconomic factors. One thing can be said without research. The events of recent years have brought significant changes and changes in the business environment, so this has not left the world of businesses untouched either. This study focuses on this very idea and approaches the issue of competitiveness through a list of literature as well as primary research findings.

articleTitle: Implement ICP Algorithm for SLAM Using Relative Motion Threshold and Robust Kernel
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) stands as a crucial technology for Autonomous Vehicles, enabling the construction of an environment map while concurrently localizing the vehicle or robot within it. Leveraging sensor data such as LiDAR and wheel odometry, the environment map is progressively developed through a scan-matching algorithm. The Iterative Closest Point (ICP) algorithm plays an important role in finding relative transformations between point clouds, ensuring robust alignment and refining map accuracy. In this paper, two novel techniques for outlier rejection are implemented: Relative Motion Threshold (RMT) and Robust Kernel. RMT detects outliers based on error threshold calculated by a ratio which depends on the convergence rate. While Robust Kernel reduce the influence of outliers. Through simulation, our findings reveal that the incorporation of RMT and Robust Kernel outperforms traditional techniques, demonstrating map-building capabilities. The application of ICP, RMT, and Robust Kernel showcases the potential for enhancing SLAM performance, promising advancements in autonomous vehicle navigation and mapping.

articleTitle: An Investigation of the Hydrochemical Parameters for Natural Monuments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Armenia, is situated amidst a rich tapestry of surface and underground water resources. Groundwater, constituting the Earth's most abundant source of fresh water, plays a pivotal role in sustaining ecosystems and human activities. This paper focuses on three natural monuments located in Vayots Dzor and addresses the pressing need for water resource preservation in Armenia. The urgency arises from the escalating mining activities and the growing demands of fish production systems. The primary objective of this study is the thorough investigation of hydrochemical parameters of hydrogeological natural monuments within Vayots Dzor. The article delineates key hydrochemical parameters of three such monuments, integral to characterizing their freshwater characteristics. A notable innovation of this paper lies in its initial attempts to gather characteristic data. Surprisingly, none of the governmental structures, including the Ministry of Nature Protection of RA, Ministry of Health of RA, and relevant regional and local authorities, possessed such data. Consequently, an information base was established for several monuments, providing not only conservation priority measures but also strategies for the effective utilization of potential destinations. The acquired data underwent pre-analysis and comparison with national standards, existing literature, and data from mineral water brands available in markets. The water sampling and analysis for the natural hydrogeological monuments—namely, “Source of Moz,” “Source of Paruyr Sevak,” and “Source of Grav”—were conducted with methodological and technical support from specialists affiliated with the “Environmental Impact Monitoring Centre” under the Ministry of Nature Protection of the RA. The findings of this study contribute not only to the understanding of the hydrochemical parameters of these natural monuments but also provide valuable insights for sustainable water resource management in the region.

articleTitle: A Design of Synergic Humanoid Robot Hand Using Finger Lock and Sensors to Achieve Adaptive Grasps
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: The complex nature of the human hand has led to many contemporary robotic hand designs using cable mechanisms to employ a minimum of five drive motors, with each motor dedicated to controlling an individual finger. This approach results in systems that are bulky and challenging to control. In response to this limitation, a novel finger drive mechanism is proposed in this study. By integrating a cable-driven pulley mechanism and a finger-locking mechanism, this new 5-finger robotic hand design requires only two drive motors instead of the conventional five. This innovative configuration not only provides robust and precise gripping force but also exhibits the ability to grasp objects of various shapes and sizes. The operational mechanism of the robotic hand is divided into three stages: pre-grasp, lock, and grip. Furthermore, sensors put on the fingertips help the system recognize when contact with an object happens, allowing it to determine when each stage begins. To validate the proposed design, a 3D-printed prototype was developed, and its motion capabilities were evaluated using simulation.

articleTitle: Response Surface Methodology to Characterize the Indicators for the Early Detection of Fraudulent Cases in the Motor Insurance Market
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: The motor liability insurance market currently has many stakeholders, so investigating potential fraud in this area takes top priority. The payments related to fraudulent claims cause, in particular, economic damage, so several solutions have been developed to detect them at an early stage. In this paper, a response surface methodology-inspired concept is introduced to estimate the theoretical assumed probability of being an insurance fraud. For that purpose, three easily and unambiguously identifiable factors have been chosen: the insurance payout, EUR; the age of the innocent participant vehicle, years; and the payment period of the insurance contract. The methodology was applied to select the parameters with the most substantial effect on the fraud risk.

articleTitle: Examining the Effect of Initial Parameter Value Choice of a Tumor Model on Gradient-Based Parameter Fitting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Cyber-medical systems are becoming more and more popular in health sciences. They help to make faster and more accurate diagnoses and create more effective and personalized treatments for patients. During our research, we use a mathematical model that describes the behavior of the tumor and the effect of the drug for therapy personalization. Our goal is to personalize the parameters in the mathematical model and optimize therapy based on this. As a result of the optimization, we aim to treat cancer with smaller doses of chemotherapy administered at more frequent intervals, resulting in milder side effects and a lower chance of developing drug resistance. In this article, we examine three parameters of the tumor model to find the parameter range of the initial values such that the identification algorithm finds the real value. We created virtual patients whose parameters were obtained by fitting a model from previous experiments; thus, the parameters are known, and the results of the identification can be evaluated.

articleTitle: Combining Genetic Algorithms And Or-Tools To Solve Flexible Job-Shop Scheduling Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Flexible job shop scheduling problems (FJSPs) require optimally assigning operations to machines and sequencing them to minimize objectives like makespan. Metaheuristics like genetic algorithms (GAs) are well-suited for large FJSPs. This study presents a combination of GAs and Google OR-Tools to solve FJSPs, with GAs generating machine assignments and OR-Tools developing schedules. Specifically, GAs first assign operations to machines, and then OR-Tools schedules the operations to minimize makespan and calculate the solution's characteristics. These characteristics inform the GA's selection, crossover, and mutation to produce improved solutions over iterations. Computational experiments on standard benchmark instances demonstrate solution quality comparable to state-of-the-art tabu search approaches. The feasibility of the algorithm to effectively solve FJSPs is thereby established. Additionally, the study introduces a viable hybrid GA for providing high-quality FJSP solutions.

articleTitle: Investigate on Skull Defect Reconstruction Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Skull reconstruction is a promising and significant research topic in patient treatment. The process involves several steps including identifying the location of skull defects, designing grafts, manufacturing grafts, and surgery. In the step of identifying the location of skull defects, we can easily determine the position thanks to images of the defective skull captured by advanced imaging technologies such as CT and MRI. During the manufacturing step, 3D printing technology makes it easy to manufacture the grafts. Skull graft surgery is the final step. The accuracy in designing the graft piece is crucial for the success of the surgical procedure. The design step of the graft is the most important, with many challenges. Previously, design was done using commercial CAD software or some online platforms. It involves a series of steps such as segmentation, noise filtering, and refinement to achieve the desired shape of the graft. The complex steps increase processing time and depend on the processing technique of the technician. This causes difficulties and prolongs the treatment process for the patient. Currently, the method of using deep learning to reconstruct graft pieces is a new approach thanks to increasingly advanced AI technology. The advantages and disadvantages of these methods will be presented and discussed in this study.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Mecanum-Kresling Wheel
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Origami has been used to design deployable systems by folding and unfolding along the crease lines. Because of its flexibility and foldability using non-rigid material, the Kresling origami pattern has been used in several designs. We create a rigid origami-inspired mechanism based on Kresling pattern with deployability and customizable collapsibility that produces a novel use in mecanum wheel design. This mechanism is deployable when collapsed and can be selectively collapsed by altering the twisting angle. The mechanical in the mecanum wheel provides direction shifting functionality while being highly deployable and collapsible. In this work, the ability to deploy the rigid Kresling mechanism into Mecanum wheel is designed and simulated in MATLAB and Solid Work.

articleTitle: Control of Continuous, High Purity Distillation Column Using Nonlinear Adaptive Control Based on Robust Fixed Point Transformation Phenomena
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: A nonlinear feedback control scheme for continuous, binary, tray, multiple-product, and high-purity distillation columns has been proposed. Vapor-liquid equilibrium curve of raw material is presented. Physical properties, kinematics, and dynamics of the distillation column are also calculated. Automatic process control technique is designed for the composition of product in order to follow a desired trajectory. Controlling is solved with a novel nonlinear, adaptive approach, called Robust Fixed Point Transformation (RFPT) as well as with the classical, linear PID controller so as to compare their performance. RFPT provides a remedy to disturbances that occur at linear process control.

articleTitle: Agile Methodology for Competitiveness
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: The adoption of agile methodology, agile philosophy, or agile project management approach is surrounded by a successful trend. However, whether this is merely a fashion and marketing ploy, or can genuinely contribute to enhancing corporate competitiveness is a more complex question. The peculiarities of agile projects in managing changes, and the interaction and communication with clients, can offer an interesting approach to the company's market presence and increasing customer satisfaction.

articleTitle: Knowledge of Cryptocurrencies and Blockchain Technology Through the Eyes of Different Generations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Digitalization has brought many changes to our lives, bringing new opportunities, ways of working and solutions. It has also deeply affected the field of finance, in particular the way payments are made. New instruments have emerged in the form of cryptocurrencies, which now number more than 23,000. Creating cryptocurrencies today is a very simple task, but it is pointless to have so many if they are not accepted and used. The aim of this study is to assess, based on the results of a non-representative questionnaire survey conducted in Hungary, the attitudes of respondents of different generations towards cryptocurrencies and the related blockchain technology. Our aim is to highlight key similarities and differences in order to provide a basis for future research by profiling users as thoroughly as possible.

articleTitle: Effects of Operating Conditions on the Performance of An Electric Assisted Bicycle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: The use of electric bicycles is one of the alternative solutions to reduce exhaust emissions from vehicles using fossil fuels. To design an electric bicycle with high-performance, the influences of operating conditions on its performance need to be considered. A simulation study is carried out to evaluate the effects of input conditions, such as rider mass, slope, and wind speed, on the motion and power required of an electric assisted bicycle. Mathematical models are created to depict the operation of the electric bicycle, including a bicycle dynamic model with rider's control, a bicycle dynamic model with the motor assistance, and a required power model to overcome the resistance forces. Based on the simulation results obtained for examining the effects of input conditions on the motion characteristics of the electric bicycle, an appropriate power could be chosen for the electric motor.

articleTitle: Adapting Self-Driving Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: The scientific investigation delves into delineating the peril presented by autonomous driving systems. Initially, an extensive literature review has been undertaken to expound upon the fundamental concepts and evaluative criteria pertinent to self-driving technology. Subsequently, a comprehensive exploration of information security and its multifaceted dimensions will be conducted. The research will further scrutinize networking and IT threats, analyzing their implications and ramifications within the context of autonomous driving systems. Ultimately, conclusions will be drawn based on the synthesis of these findings, offering insights into the overarching threat landscape posed by self-driving engines

articleTitle: Perceptions of Local Macroeconomic Challenges Faced by Hungarian Enterprises and How to Meet Them Along Competitiveness Dimensions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: The 2000s held many challenges for humanity. The 2008 mortgage crisis significantly redrawn our financial thinking and changed our attitudes towards financial products. The effects that thousands of people have suffered as a result of poorly made financial decisions have contributed to all these processes. The same characteristics could be said for businesses. Following the mortgage crisis, we became acquainted with a number of other financial crises during the 2000s, but a new level after all this was still the coronavirus epidemic escalated in 2020 and the ensuing crisis. The growing digitalisation challenge, the advancement of artificial intelligence, and the automation of processes are causing headaches for many small and medium-sized enterprises. Businesses around the world face these challenges, sometimes stronger and weaker. The aim of our study is to present the local, macroeconomic challenges and the assessment of those whose competitiveness is affected and influenced by the results of a questionnaire research conducted in Hungary. The research is part of an international survey, in our present study we want to present the effects in Hungary.

articleTitle: Impact Determination Exercise in Cyber Security Assessments of Industrial Automation and Control Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: The demand for improving the cyber security of Industry Automation and Control Systems (IACS) is increasing significantly, and this increase causes a shortage of available security resources. In future more cyber security projects shall be made with less resources. For this reason, the efficiency of IACS cyber security projects is under constant pressure to be improved. One way of doing that is selecting the right target: paying more attention on the protection of impactful systems, where a lot can be protected with cyber security investments; and paying less attention on improving cyber security of systems with low impact. Priorities are not always obvious, and even at the first glance obvious priorities are sometimes misleading. The best way to have accurate and reliable information about the impact of a cyber security incident on a control system is having a certain level of understanding of the process and the role of the given system in that process. This research outlines an Impact Determination Exercise, which helps accurately estimate the possible impacts of an IACS cyber security incident by assessing the business process of a plant.

articleTitle: Anomaly Detection of Time Series Containing Tumor Volumes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Optimizing chemotherapy treatments often involves customizing drug dosages for individuals or groups with similar traits. This process relies on converting individual patient charac-teristics into mathematical parameters in a tumor model. Mathematical tumor models are thus used for treatment generation; the models are validated and tuned (i.e., their parameters are identified) based on measurements. Consequently, the accuracy of these measurements is essential, as any errors or excessive noise in the measured tumor volumes can significantly impact the model parameters. This paper uses two different approaches for filtering outliers in the time series of tumor volumes. During the first approach, we constructed an equation based on the differences in the time series, while the second approach was based on autoencoders. The calculated metrics indicated greater accuracy for the first method; nevertheless, the neural network-based approach is more universally applicable. In the future, a combination of these methods can be applied to tumor measurements before identifying the parameters of the experimental mice.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Analysis and Solutions for Enhancing SCADA Systems Security in Critical Infrastructures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems security is a critical infrastructure issue, not only to maintain service continuity in the face of hostile and cyber-terrorist assaults but also to assure the resilience and integrity of processes and operations. In addition to security vulnerabilities at the system level, SCADA protocols are frequently inherently susceptible. They may lack key security precautions. Contrary to that, they often depend on “security by obscurity” or isolation from public networks. Without security methodologies like encryption and authentication, the underlying protocols present a convenient attack vector for hackers attempting to compromise SCADA devices. The authors bring attention to the security concerns and unresolved matters involving SCADA devices, showcasing the significance of enhancing their security. Furthermore, the paper evaluates SCADA networks, going beyond that to deliberate on the security measures accessible for countering attacks on SCADA networks.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Analysis of IOTS Tools
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: In an era marked by rapid technological evolution, the advent of 5G networks heralds a transformative leap in telecommunications, promising to redefine our digital interactions with its unparalleled speed and connectivity. This breakthrough, however, is accompanied by growing concerns over IT security, as highlighted in the comprehensive research conducted by Patrik Viktor and Monika Fodor from Obuda University. Their study delves into the nuanced perceptions and attitudes toward IT security and 5G networks across different generational cohorts, employing a quantitative approach through a rigorously pre-tested standardized questionnaire. The investigation, which gathered insights from 443 evaluable questionnaires, uncovers notable generational disparities in the understanding of IT security threats and the emphasis on human factors within IT security frameworks. The research reveals that, despite the advanced technological landscape 5G networks introduce, there exists a prevalent sense of uncertainty regarding their security implications across all surveyed generational groups. This uncertainty underscores the complexity of integrating 5G technology into existing IT infrastructures and highlights the critical need for targeted educational initiatives and policy developments tailored to address these generational nuances in IT security awareness. Viktor and Fodor's findings underscore the pivotal role of networks in modern society, not merely as technological infrastructures but as fundamental components of human connectivity. The study emphasizes the importance of a multi-layered approach to cybersecurity, integrating technological solutions with an acute awareness of human behavior's role in maintaining secure digital environments. As we stand on the threshold of widespread 5G deployment, this research offers invaluable insights into the generational perspectives shaping our understanding of IT security in the age of 5G, advocating for a holistic strategy that combines comprehensive cybersecurity measures with human-centric considerations to navigate the impending challenges and opportunities. 5G network impact, IOT, Snowball.

articleTitle: Are Cross-Asset Spillovers Evidence of an Anti-Equilibrium? An Analysis of the S&P500 Index and Brent Crude Oil Prices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: This study draws parallels between the theory of reflexivity and classical economics and attempts to find some evidence of the phenomena using Diebold and Yilmaz's spillover methodology. The closest form of perfect competition exists in the stock market. We find support to the idea that stock prices affect the fundamental value of companies (in the energy sector at least) thanks to the non-zero spillover effect between seemingly uncorrelated markets.

articleTitle: Comparison of Commercial and Open Source ETL Tools
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: The extraction, transformation, and loading (ETL) process is a critical component in data integration. This article conducts a comprehensive comparative analysis between commercial and open source ETL tools, shedding light on their respective attributes, benefits, and drawbacks. The objective is to facilitate data professionals and organizations in making well-informed decisions when selecting ETL tools tailored to their specific requirements. This comparison meticulously assesses both commercial and open source ETL tools, scrutinizing aspects including functionality, performance, scalability, user-friendliness, and extensibility. Furthermore, it considers the ecosystem encompassing these tools, such as available connectors, plugins, and contributions from the community. Real-world case studies and practical user experiences are analyzed to furnish actionable insights into the strengths and limitations of each ETL tool category. Ultimately, the choice between commercial and open source ETL tools hinges on project-specific requisites, financial constraints, and the degree of customization sought. The survey shows that open-source tools can compete with those intended for the commercial market, especially for smaller companies or individual users.

articleTitle: The Role of Digitalisation in Strengthening the Competitiveness of Education
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Digitalisation is the defining concept of the 21st century. Today, there is no area of life that is not digitised, not connected to the internet in some way, not connected to an online platform where the actor or solution is available. Digitalisation cannot be excluded from the education system either. Higher education has long taken advantage of the opportunities offered by digitisation, which greatly facilitates the lives of individuals involved in education. It is an effective and good solution for the educators, but it is also an equally effective and good solution for the learners. In this study, we want to assess the impact of digitalisation on the competitiveness of education and the perceptions of those involved in education, students and learners. We want to assess how the competitiveness of education as a key area can be improved by moving part of education from the physical space to the digital space and how this is received by those involved in education. In this paper, we will present our findings and the context that determines and judges the current state of the art of this issue based on the results of a Hungarian primary research.

articleTitle: Data Collection Studies for the Better Understanding of Factors in Type 1 Diabetes Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: This paper describes clinical trials which are aimed to understand the relationship between blood glucose level changes and physical activity in type 1 diabetics. Also, the paper introduces our study, including the protocol and preliminary statistics on the collected data. Our study observes type 1 diabetic individuals in everyday living conditions.
