During the study, the subjects log their insulin intake, physiological status (circadian rhythm, menstruation, stress), nutrient and fluid intake, and medication intake by means of electronic diaries. In addition, heart rate is automatically collected from a wearable device. The data will be used to investigate the effect of physical activity on blood glucose levels, e.g. for virtual patient system model development (“digital twin”), to develop and refine physical activity detection, and to refine blood glucose prediction.

articleTitle: Ensemble Learning for Modeling Luminance in Plasmonic Nanoellipse for Tunable Spaser
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: in a recent study we provided a theoretical framework for plasmonic coupled elliptical nanostructure capable of producing high-intensity spasers or nanolasers. The nanostructure which consists of a gold film substrate, underwent testing for various light polarizations where we selected a simple elliptical shape and then modified it to explore different geometries. The structure exhibited strong coupled resonance modes, particularly localized surface plasmon (LSP). Through finite-element method (FEM) simulations, we investigated the localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) of the system. Results revealed that introducing symmetry-breaking techniques, such as creating a symmetry-broken nano-ellipse (SBE), significantly increased both LSPR peaks and local field intensity (LFI). By selecting appropriate gain media, the nanostructure could support various plasmonic resonance modes across different wavelengths. Moreover, it demonstrated potential for developing a compact nanolaser with a broad tunability range. Adjusting light polarization and making structural modifications led to the observation of Surface Plasmon Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation (SPASER) phenomena. The proposed model, with its substantial LSPR values, shows promise for applications like surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy and sensing. The application of the data-driven methods in modeling the above phenomena has not been explored yet. Due to the complex nature of the phenomena, it is expected that the data-driven models can provide promising results. Consequently, in this article the primary results of proposing ensemble machine learning in modeling the above phenomenon are presented. In this work random forest (RF) and support vector machine (SVM) were employed for modeling and analysis of outcomes.

articleTitle: Efficient Generative AI-Assisted Academic Research: Considerations for a Research Model Proposal
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GAl) has improved significantly since the emergence of ChatGPT 3.5 and is becoming an indispensable tool for many scholars, teachers, and students. This article addresses the main pitfalls of using GAl in research and academic writing, such as AI bias, AI hallucination, and ethical issues with literature review. It also provides an overview of how publishers view the use of GAl in academic writing. Finally, it offers some recommendations to address AI bias and AI hallucination problems, while maintaining the productivity benefits of using GAl. It also outlines a model that would enable efficient use of GAl in research and academic writing.

articleTitle: Navigating the Digital Frontier: Exploration of Education Digitalization in Africa
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: The pandemic period caused by COVID has transformed our everyday life, and the use of more advanced technologies have become necessary. Around the world, as yet unknown innovations and developments have surfaced and we are reshaping everything we do, from global corporations to simple activities, we do everything. This paper examines the digitalization of education, with a particular focus on the African continent. It will first describe the educational systems and tools used in the past, then examine the emergence of digitalization and its effects and impacts. In addition, we will present hypothetical solutions that may be beneficial and practical to implement, examine their benefits, and consider the difficulties and obstacles that must be eliminated for this new innovation to enter the educational bloodstream of the Africa. Finally, conclusions and recommendations will be made.

articleTitle: From Deep Learning to ChatGPT for Materials Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) provide competitive advantages to various fields of research. This survey explores the journey from using deep learning to adopting ChatGPT in materials design. It covers how methodologies have shifted, moving away from traditional deep learning models to embracing LLMs such as ChatGPT, in advancing materials design research. The focus is on methods and applications, highlighting how LLMs are shaping the landscape of materials design. The survey aims to provide insights into the essential role of ChatGPT in this domain, offering a comprehensive view of its methods and diverse applications.

articleTitle: Startups and Mediation - Trust for Our Future Commitments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: It is possible to form cooperations in peace and in a peaceful way. We are not talking about forced agreements or forced compromises, since money is also a central issue from the point of view of the research topic. Does the dreamer of the idea receive funding from his cooperations? Cooperation is not an independent and, even more so, not a self-explanatory and self-operating process. It requires continuous expression, activity, proactivity and cooperation from all those involved in the process.

articleTitle: Social Media's Impact: Influencing Purchases, Shaping Choices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 11th International Conference on Computational Cybernetics and Cyber-Medical Systems (ICCC)
abstract: Social media has revolutionized communication and interaction, leading to a growing interest in understanding its impact on consumer behavior and purchasing decisions. Its impact on consumer behavior is studied using a mixed methods approach. The research explores how social media influences purchasing decisions, shopping habits, and trends. Quantitative method is applied, data analysis, existing research, and consumer surveys reveal key drivers like price, quality despite influencer and celebrity recommendations. Findings show increased spending and brand switching among buyers influenced by social media. This study offers valuable insights for stakeholders like platforms, businesses to optimize their strategies, shareholders evaluating social media investments, and consumers.
